issue: ALT 147 U/L (4.2x ULN) at Week 12 on 2014-04-18, with no matching adverse event recorded; all other ALT values were normal.
query_text: The Week 12 laboratory result on 2014-04-18 shows ALT of 147 U/L (reference range 6–35 U/L; about 4.2x ULN), flagged HIGH. ALT was 30 U/L at Week 8 (2014-03-24) and 25 U/L at Week 16 (2014-05-19), and AST and total bilirubin were within range on 2014-04-18. No adverse event for this elevation is recorded. Please confirm whether the investigator considers this result clinically significant and, if so, record it as an adverse event with onset date, severity, relationship and outcome. If not, please confirm it was reviewed and judged not clinically significant, or tell us if the value was entered in error.

issue: Two INCREASED APPETITE records have the same start and end dates, but their outcomes conflict, and one says NOT RECOVERED despite having an end date.
query_text: There are two adverse event records for INCREASED APPETITE, both starting 2014-01-29 and ending 2014-07-16, both mild and with relationship REMOTE. One record (AE 1) gives the outcome as NOT RECOVERED/NOT RESOLVED even though it has an end date of 2014-07-16. The other (AE 8) gives RECOVERED/RESOLVED. Please confirm whether these are the same event entered twice. If so, please delete the duplicate. Please also make the outcome and end date agree (an event with an end date would normally be recorded as resolved).

issue: The Screening 1 laboratory collection date (2013-12-31) is 20 days before the recorded Screening 1 visit date (2014-01-20).
query_text: The laboratory samples linked to the SCREENING 1 visit (for example ALT, AST and bilirubin) have a collection date of 2013-12-31 12:20. The SCREENING 1 visit is recorded as 2014-01-20. Please check the lab collection date and the visit date and correct whichever is wrong. If the samples really were collected on 2013-12-31, please confirm which visit they belong to.
